requirements.statement: Stand-alone BBP branding; copy and re/unbrand useful shapes; do not import foreign brand packages into integrity.
Zero variance: every changing action is prescribed and gated.
Every step/action has a hard gate with complete/incomplete outcome only.
Every boundary declares hard input, output, and failure mode (error return, throw, or process exit).
Every requirement has a binary met/not-met audit.
Binding matrix unbound entries fail audit and are listed.
Promote-only-when-bindable; in-force unbindable entries fail audit and are listed.
Practice integrity principles P1–P7 are in force.
Every published requirement appears in the binding matrix with an audit id.
Unbound matrix entries fail; report lists them.
In-force unbindable requirements fail; report lists them.
Every prescribed step has a hard gate with complete/incomplete criteria.
Every public boundary declares input, output, and failure mode.
If breaking the rule would make *this noun* a lie, the rule lives on the noun, as an adjective or as a verb precondition/postcondition.
If the work spans nouns, I/O, other goals, or a business outcome, it is a goal.

Cross-noun work does not get glued onto the most convenient noun. `allocatePaymentToInvoices` is a goal, or a `PaymentAllocation` noun if it has its own adjectives. It is not `Invoice.allocateAcrossFriends`.
If a verb does not need the noun’s adjective set, it does not belong on the noun.
Noun fields are private. No goal, adapter, or other noun writes them.
The only legal mutation of a noun is a public verb on that noun.
Nouns never call goals. Direction is goal → (goal public entrypoint | noun-verb) plus explicit reads. A durable engine may host a goal; it is not a caller above the goal layer.
Goals may read what the noun chooses to expose (queries / snapshots). Goals may not reach through that snapshot and write.
Every public goal entrypoint has an input contract and an output contract.
Every public noun-verb has an input contract and an output contract.
A field that means the same thing in two contracts is defined once and referenced. Duplicate independent definitions of the same meaning are a defect.
Contracts are versioned. Breaking changes require a new version and an ADR.
One public entrypoint per goal.
A goal may call another goal only through that goal's public entrypoint and contract. Goal internals are not importable.
Shared domain logic that protects a noun lives on the noun, not in a helper copied into two goals.
A new goal is created only when there is a distinct use-case. Do not create a goal per function (`ValidateEmail` as a sibling of `CreateCustomer` unless it is a real standalone capability).
Goals may call goals through public contracts. There is no separate workflow citizen. A durable runtime hosts a goal; it does not replace the goal.

Compensation and retries live in the calling goal (and its runtime if durable), not inside the noun, unless the noun's adjective itself requires idempotency of a verb. Verbs must be safe to retry if a durable goal retries them. Declare that on the verb.
Do not maintain a separate hand-authored execution-graph file that duplicates a durable goal's runtime definition.
The charter, contracts, and code must agree. If they disagree, the build fails. Code does not win by existing. Spec does not win by being newer. They must be reconciled in the same change.
Dependency and impact information is generated from code and contracts, not authored as a parallel JSON document.
ADRs that are superseded are marked superseded, not deleted. The trail is part of integrity.
A gate fails the change if a goal or adapter assigns a noun field or imports a noun internals module.
A gate fails the change if invoice-equivalent money math, status transitions, or named adjectives appear outside the owning noun (copy-paste of the adjective).
Tests for a noun’s adjectives live next to the noun and run on every verb. Goal tests do not replace them.
A sensitive adjective listed in taint.txt may cross one boundary: the consuming verb.
Noun state is not mutated through non-OO escape hatches from outside a published verb.
Change class (A–F) is stated.
Adjectives live on the noun named in C1, not in a goal folder.
New orchestration lives in a goal, not as a method on an unrelated noun.
No assignment to noun fields occurs outside the noun module.
Every state change of a noun goes through a public verb.
No noun module imports a goal module.
Each changed public goal has input and output schemas.
Each changed public verb has input and output schemas.
Shared meanings use a shared type; no forked `balance` / `status` / `currency`.
Breaking schema changes have a new version and an ADR.
Each changed goal has exactly one public entrypoint.
No goal imports another goal’s internals.
No new goal exists whose only job is a single noun-verb with no I/O or policy — or an ADR explains why the wrapper exists.
Goal-to-goal calls use public entrypoints only; no imports of another goal's internals.
Verbs invoked from a retrying (durable) goal are idempotent, or the caller uses an idempotency key the verb honors.
Every adjective named in the proposal has a test on the noun.
Every new verb has tests for success, precondition failure, and adjective preservation.
Goal tests cover the use-case, not a copy of the noun’s adjective suite.
No second implementation of the same adjective exists in the diff (search for duplicated predicates).
Fitness / lint rules for R23 and R24 passed.
Impact list in the proposal matches generated callers of the changed verbs/goals.
Charter/ADR/code/contracts were updated in the same change if they were affected.
Adversarial review findings are all fixed or explicitly rebutted.
Ratification is recorded for classes that require it.
Sensitive adjectives fetched in a unit are not returned, stored, or passed across another boundary.
No __dict__ / vars() / exec() / eval() mutates noun state from outside a published verb.
Every agent noun has an identity file that states purpose and adjectives.
Every verb on an agent noun has an input contract, output contract, and failure mode.
Every agent noun declares handoff-in (preconditions) and completion artifact (postconditions).
Success criteria are binary: ops (work completed as specified) vs defects (deviation from spec or adjectives).
Produce ≠ Audit ≠ Ship. An agent may not audit its own output as the final gate.
Audit roles have no ship verbs. Adversarial auditors produce findings; another role decides.
Agent noun has identity and adjectives.
Each verb has input, output, and failure mode.
Handoff-in and completion artifact are declared.
Success criteria are binary (ops vs defects).
Produce ≠ Audit ≠ Ship separation is honored.
Audit roles have no ship verbs.

Produce→fitness handoff is default-closed. Produce completion requires change artifacts AND produce package. Without a complete package, fitness preflight returns handoff_refused; content scoring does not open.
Produce package present before fitness; incomplete handoffs refused, not soft-failed.

Produce packages require task/board SSOT exit evidence. Packages must include ssot_leaf_ids (one or more opaque leaf ids from the task/board SSOT) and ssot_exit_status (non-empty exit state string). Missing SSOT exit evidence triggers handoff_refused; fitness scoring refuses MET; adversarial audit refuses PASS (P-020).
Task/board SSOT exit evidence present in produce package (ssot_leaf_ids + ssot_exit_status); missing evidence refused (P-020).
Quality evidence required at fitness. Every produce package submitted to fitness preflight must include quality evidence from prior gate executions.
Quality evidence required at adversarial audit. Every artifact submitted to adversarial audit must have quality evidence traceable to SSOT.
Quality snapshot recorded at boundary exit. Every boundary exit that advances work must record a quality snapshot.
Defect classification is binary. Every opportunity outcome is classified as exactly one of: op or defect.
Quality metric is ops/opportunities. The canonical quality formula; no alternative weighted or continuous formulas.
Quality evidence present in produce package (gate receipts with outcome + timestamp).
Quality snapshot recorded at boundary exit ({ opportunities, ops, defects, quality }).
